_README: The hypothesis inventory: principles the library ASSUMES rather than
proves, threaded through binders instead of axioms. A conditional theorem
is unconditionally provable, so #print axioms sees nothing -- these are
axioms wearing different clothes, and this registry is where each one is
adjudicated. tools/hypotheses.py counts every declaration assuming each
(binder position) and every one concluding in it, and fails on a
registered name that no longer occurs anywhere.
kind: 'principle'  -- a Prop with logical strength (the lattice's kind);
'readout'    -- Type-level data ABOUT an object, demandable of every
object, the cousin of a principle;
'witness'    -- Type-level data supplying an EXISTENTIAL's witness,
where a readout supplies a DISJUNCTION's branch: an
existential withholding a scale against a disjunction
withholding a bit;
'decider'    -- Type-level data carrying a PROMISE about a predicate,
so its strength varies with the predicate and there
may be no single principle to record;
'structural' -- a blanket mathematical hypothesis that scopes a
theory (uniform continuity, detachability).
kind is VALIDATED against exactly these five. It was displayed and never
compared for the registry's whole life, and four entries drifted to a
fifth value nothing defined.
discharge: what removing the hypothesis would take, or why it stays.
calibration: pins the hypothesis to its strength. shape: 'omniscience' |
'choice' | 'modulus' | 'subject'; principle: a lattice node or 'none';
forward: theorem deriving the hypothesis from the principle; reverse:
theorem recovering the principle from the hypothesis schema; 'open' marks
a direction owed, 'n/a' one that does not apply. _uncalibrated counts
entries owing (no block, or an open direction) and must be met exactly.
